title: implement make_rays_1d

atoms.evidence: rays = t.zeros((num_pixels, 2, 3), dtype=t.float32) — preallocate, then fill via slice assignment
t.linspace(-y_limit, y_limit, num_pixels, out=rays[:, 1, 1]) — explicit Tip cell calls out out= kwarg as the lesson
rays[:, 1, 0] = 1 and the rays[:, 1, 1] view target of linspace; Tip explains 'basic indexing returns a view that shares storage'
intro markdown defines R(u)=O+uD; here the learner only fills in O=(0,0,0) and a D pointing at x=1 — no math on the form itself

notes: First tagged part1 exercise. Cleanest possible 'preallocate + view-fill' triplet (zeros-init + linspace-out + slice-view-mutation). The Tip cell is unusually explicit about which atoms are being taught — it names out= and view-mutation directly. ray-parametric-form is marked incidental because the exercise is mechanical (set last dim to ramp, set first dim to 1) rather than reasoning about the parametric form.
